subject: Intermittent 429s in production — urgent remediation plan
messages:
From: Dina Shah <dina@opalhealth.com>
To: Jordan Blake <jordan.blake@redwood.ai>
Cc: Opal Health Platform <platform@opalhealth.com>
Date: Sun, 18 Oct 2026 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Sudden 429s from our production traffic (urgent)

Hi Jordan,

Starting ~08:30PT this morning our production integration began receiving a high rate of 429s from Redwood. We've seen a spike from our usual 0.1% to ~12% fail-rate across multiple endpoints (generation and embeddings).

Sample request ids: req-6932, req-6937, req-6941 — attached a short list with timestamps. This is impacting our nightly sync and a portion of user-facing flows. Can you please triage ASAP?

We are on the OPH-4382 committed tier and haven't changed our usage pattern. Please advise next steps and whether we should fail-over.

Thanks,
Dina
Dina Shah
Senior Platform Engineer, Opal Health
From: Jordan Blake <jordan.blake@redwood.ai>
To: Dina Shah <dina@opalhealth.com>
Cc: Neha Kapoor <neha.kapoor@redwood.ai>, Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwood.ai>, Lauren Bishop <lauren.bishop@redwood.ai>
Date: Sun, 18 Oct 2026 09:28:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Sudden 429s from our production traffic (urgent)

Thanks for the heads up, Dina — I'm sorry you're hitting this. I've looped in our infra and support leads (Marcus, Lauren) to triage immediately.

Immediate plan:
- Marcus to capture traces and check quota mapping.
- We'll validate whether this is tenant-level or project-level enforcement.
- Temporary mitigation: if safe, we can bump a tenant override to bring you back online while we fix the mapping.

I'll follow up within 30–45 minutes with next steps.

-Jordan
Jordan Blake
Account Executive, Redwood Inference
From: Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwood.ai>
To: Jordan Blake <jordan.blake@redwood.ai>, Neha Kapoor <neha.kapoor@redwood.ai>
Cc: Lauren Bishop <lauren.bishop@redwood.ai>, Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>
Date: Sun, 18 Oct 2026 09:47:00 -07:00
Subject: RE: Sudden 429s from our production traffic (urgent)

Quick update from infra: we see repeated 429s with enforcement point = tenant-cap; however the tenant_id on those enforcement events maps to a shared quota entity that shouldn't include OPH. Preliminary root cause: a recent config-migration job (2026-10-15) introduced a mapping regression where Opal Health's org_id was associated with a pooled quota used for internal testing.

What I did so far:
- Pulled enforcement logs and matched them to Dina's sample request ids (attached: opal-429-samples.txt).
- Created a rollback patch for the mapping table to reassign Opal Health to their committed quota row.
- Prepared a temporary tenant override (+40% for 2 hours) we can apply if Opal gives the go-ahead.

Risks: low — change is a config mapping rewrite (small table) that is reversible. We'll monitor token counters and throttle windows during the change.

Next: Marcus will coordinate a brief maintenance window to apply the rollback and monitor.

Attachments: redwood-diagnostics-OPH-4382.zip
From: Jordan Blake <jordan.blake@redwood.ai>
To: Dina Shah <dina@opalhealth.com>
Cc: Neha Kapoor <neha.kapoor@redwood.ai>, Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwood.ai>, Lauren Bishop <lauren.bishop@redwood.ai>
Date: Sun, 18 Oct 2026 10:10:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Sudden 429s from our production traffic (urgent)

Dina — thanks to Marcus for the quick root-cause work. TL;DR: a config migration mistakenly attached your org to a pooled testing quota, causing tenant-level enforcement to throttle you.

Proposal (same message sent in the thread so all stakeholders have it):
1) With your permission we'll apply a temporary override (+40%) immediately to bring traffic back while we deploy the mapping rollback (expected ~5–10 minutes to apply).
2) Marcus will monitor for 30 minutes post-change and confirm restored success rates.
3) We'll share a formal incident write-up and a credit estimate; Neha, I'll coordinate the credits.

If you approve, reply "please proceed" and we'll run mitigation now.

Also attaching a quick credit estimate sheet so you know what to expect if there is measurable disruption.

-Jordan
From: Dina Shah <dina@opalhealth.com>
To: Jordan Blake <jordan.blake@redwood.ai>
Cc: Opal Health Platform <platform@opalhealth.com>
Date: Sun, 18 Oct 2026 10:13:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Sudden 429s from our production traffic (urgent)

Thanks — please proceed with the temporary override and the mapping rollback. We prefer the change to be done now to minimize user impact. Please post updates to this thread and include an ETA to full resolution.

—Dina
From: Jordan Blake <jordan.blake@redwood.ai>
To: Dina Shah <dina@opalhealth.com>
Cc: Neha Kapoor <neha.kapoor@redwood.ai>, Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwood.ai>, Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>, Lauren Bishop <lauren.bishop@redwood.ai>
Date: Thu, 21 Oct 2026 17:05:00 -07:00
Subject: RE: Sudden 429s from our production traffic (urgent) — resolution and next steps

Dina — closing the loop after remediation and verification. Summary:
- 2026-10-18 10:15PT: applied temporary +40% tenant override and rolled back the config-mapping.
- 10:25PT: enforcement logs show success rate returned to baseline (<0.5% 429s).
- Root cause: migration job 2026-10-15 incorrectly assigned Opal Health's org_id to an internal pooled quota row.

What we did for immediate mitigation:
- Reassigned org_id to committed quota entry and removed the pooled-test association.
- Applied short-duration override to prevent user impact while the change propagated.
- Scanned for other tenants affected by the same migration; no other customers showed the same mapping error.

Next steps and asks:
- Incident postmortem (internal) is filed: https://redwood.atlassian.net/browse/INF-7729 — we'll share the public summary and timeline by Friday 2026-10-22.
- Neha will send a billing credit estimate; Jordan will follow up with formal credit and the public-facing root-cause note for your legal/ops teams.
- Marcus and Lauren are adding a validation check into the config-migration pipeline to prevent mapping regressions.

Apologies for the disruption. We know reliability is table-stakes and appreciate your patience. Please let me know if you still see any errors or if you'd like a brief technical postmortem call.

Regards,
Jordan Blake
Account Executive, Redwood Inference
